statements.t: Kratos intends to pursue program and contract opportunities as the prime or lead contractor when we believe our probability of win is high and any investment required by Kratos is within our capital resource comfort level.

We intend to partner and team with a large, traditional system integrator or other defense technology companies when our assessment of probability of win is greater or required investment is beyond Kratos comfort level.

Investments related to the Company’s Prometheus venture with RAFAEL Advanced Defense Systems, Ltd and the new turbofan production facility in Oklahoma related to our arrangement with GE Aerospace are expected to ramp up in 2026 and 2027.

The FY 2027 defense budget proposal and the 2026 supplemental funding request are subject to Congressional approval, and it is not assured when or if they will be enacted at the levels proposed or that increases in funding will result in increased orders for either the industry or our programs.
fiscal year 2027 appropriations bills has been enacted, and we expect the continuing resolution to be extended beyond December 11, 2026.

We believe continued budget and deficit funding pressures (which are expected), CRs (which are expected), future Federal Government debt ceiling issues (which are expected), and potential Federal Government shutdowns or disruptions could have serious negative consequences for the security of our country and the defense industrial base, including the Company and related customers, employees, suppliers, investors,…

Such a dynamic and challenging federal, DoW and National Security related budgetary environment may negatively impact our customers, partners, suppliers, business and programs, and could have a material adverse effect on our forecasts, estimates, financial position, results of operations and/or cash flows.

To mitigate the impact of certain delays, we have implemented advanced and larger lot purchases of certain materials and parts where we can and practical, which has resulted in an increased use of our working capital, which is expected to continue.

In addition, inflation and the related increased costs of inputs needed to execute our business, including materials, parts, supplies, consultants, subcontractors, vendors, etc., have significantly increased our business costs and have adversely impacted our operations, profit margins and financial forecasts.
For the three months ended September 27, 2026 and September 28, 2025, the Company utilized the annual effective tax rate method based on the forecasted information provided.
For the nine months ended September 27, 2026 and September 28, 2025, the Company utilized the annual effective tax rate method based on the forecasted information provided.
We expect to recognize approximately 16% of the remaining total backlog as revenue in fiscal year 2026, an additional 50% in fiscal year 2027 and the balance thereafter.
Total backlog is our estimate of the amount of revenue expected to be realized over the remaining life of awarded contracts and task orders that we have in hand as of the measurement date.

Total backlog can include award fees, incentive fees, or other variable consideration estimated based on the most likely amount we expect to be entitled to receive, to the extent that it is probable that a significant reversal of cumulative revenue recognized will not occur.

Accordingly, we disclose the transaction price allocated to all unsatisfied or partially unsatisfied performance obligations, including those with an original expected duration of one year or less and those that include variable consideration dependent on future events.

We define funded backlog as estimated future revenue under government contracts and task orders for which funding has been appropriated by Congress and authorized for expenditure by the applicable agency, plus an estimate of the future revenue expected to be realized from commercial contracts that are under firm orders.
Because many factors affect the scheduling of projects, no assurance can be given as to when or if revenue will be realized on projects included in our backlog.
Accordingly, based on historical customer usage or operational tempo, we have reasonable expectations or visibility of what ultimate orders for Kratos’ systems, products and solutions will be.
We do not include these expected amounts in our backlog until a related contract award is received.
We do not currently intend to repatriate these earnings.

Our DSO's are impacted by the achievement of contractual billing milestones, including equipment shipments and deliveries on certain products, the receipt of contractual funding, and for certain flight requirements that must be fulfilled on certain programs, or final milestone billings which are not due until completion on certain projects, and therefore we are unable to contractually bill for amounts outstanding…

We expect our capital expenditures for fiscal year 2026 to continue to be significant for investments we are making, including in our US business totaling approximately $30 to $35 million, including approximately $20 to $25 million for Kratos owned capital aerial drones and related support equipment.

The Company is currently producing or anticipates producing several versions of the Valkyrie within the ongoing 24 unit production run, with differing versions based on routine communications with the customers, which mix and ultimate duration of the 24 Lot Build may change as a result.

In light of increased customer demand for our Firejet drones, which we expect will require us to approximately triple Firejet manufacturing capacity in Oklahoma City by the end of 2027, we are extending the timing of our previously planned Valkyrie production ramp of up to approximately 40 aircraft annually, which we previously expected to achieve by the beginning of 2028.

Both the Valkyrie and Firejet are manufactured in our Oklahoma drone facility, and with the significant expected near-term demand for Firejet, we are managing our resources and capital across our drone portfolio based on evolving customer demand, mix and timing.
The Company expects to fund approximately $25 to $35 million to the Prometheus joint venture during 2026.

If the conditions in our industry deteriorate or our customers cancel or postpone projects or if we are unable to sufficiently increase our revenues or further reduce our expenses, we may experience a significant long-term negative impact to our financial results and cash flows from operations.
The process of identifying and valuing intangible assets requires significant management judgment and the use of estimates, including projected future cash flows and appropriate discount rates.

We will continue to evaluate the provisional amounts recognized for these acquisitions at each reporting period during the measurement period to determine if any adjustments are necessary based on new information obtained about facts and circumstances that existed as of the acquisition dates.
We expect to refine these provisional amounts as the formal valuation processes for both acquisitions progresses.

statements.t: Also importantly, we reported an Adjusted EBITDA profit and margin in the third quarter of $50.9 million or 10.8 percent, demonstrating leverage of the business as production quantities increase and as Kratos continues to scale, which we expect to continue into 2027.”

DeMarco continued, “We have provided our initial full fiscal year 2027 financial forecast, including revenue of $2.1 to $2.2 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $230 to $240 million, reflecting growth of approximately 18 percent to 22 percent over our current increased 2026 financial guidance revenue range with forecasted increased 2027 margins, consistent with our previous expectations.
Our 2027 financial forecast considers that U.S. defense funding is currently operating under an extended Continuing Resolution, and, similar to 2026 and other prior years,

we expect Kratos’ third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2027 to reflect substantially greater revenue and Adjusted EBITDA assuming annual appropriations are then in place, with Q1 2027 currently expected to be our lightest fiscal quarter as a result of the CR.”

We are providing our 2026 fourth quarter guidance, tightening our full year 2026 Revenue estimate range and increasing our Adjusted EBITDA guidance, and we are providing our initial 2027 financial forecast.
Our financial guidance and forecast provided today includes certain assumptions, including and as related to:
We currently expect the existing CR to be extended beyond December 11, 2026, and at least into the first fiscal quarter of 2027.
Accordingly, the financial guidance we are providing today includes the expectation of a CR into the first Kratos fiscal quarter of 2027.

Our financial guidance and forecast provided today includes our current forecasted business mix, our expectations for employee sourcing, hiring and retention; our expectations for potential manufacturing, production and supply chain adequacy and certain potential disruptions; our expectations for the ability to adequately and on a timely basis source raw materials, parts, components, etc., the potential for parts…
We currently expect to continue to make significant investments in bid, proposal and other new program and opportunity areas, and we expect to continue to increase staffing to enable us to

We also expect to continue to make significant investments in inventory, property, plant, equipment and facilities, consistent with the Department of War’s (DoW) National Security Strategy, the DoW’s reindustrialization initiatives and the DoW’s expectations for U.S.

Kratos’ revised 2026 guidance and our 2027 forecast also assumes certain investments in our Hypersonic, Rocket System, Turbine Technology and Unmanned Systems businesses, including as related to the procurement of rocket motors, jet engines, UAVs and related systems, all of which are expected to continue to impact our operating and free cash flow as we invest in the business.

Our fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2027 cash flow estimates also include current expected working capital requirements as related to the procurement of the materials, components and equipment to increase production of turbo jet engines up to 3,000 engines produced in 2027 and potentially up to 5,000 additional engines produced in 2028, to address expected customer demand for jet engines for small cruise missiles and drones.
Our 2027 Forecast assumes that we will sell to customers approximately 1,500 turbo jet engines in 2027, with the significant majority of these deliveries occurring in the second half of 2027.

Our 2027 Forecast also includes our assumptions to begin to procure the inventory, materials and components required to produce turbofan jet engines for missiles and drones, which we also currently expect future customer contractual demand for.

We expect to continue ordering inventory, components and materials required to increase the production of Kratos Valkyries and other jet drone systems throughout 2027, with the mix of expected customer drone orders potentially changing from our current expectations, and potentially impacting the mix and numbers of drones we produce, including Valkyrie.
We also expect to continue to produce certain Kratos-owned capital drone systems and related derivatives and vehicles.

Kratos’ Space and Satellite business currently has a significant new opportunity pipeline that we are pursuing, including a substantial number of large opportunities wherein Kratos, if successful, will be the prime program system integrator.

Forecasted internally funded investments, certain of which are expected to continue into or throughout 2027 include our funding of the Prometheus joint venture, our Anaconda radar facility and program, our Helios hypersonic and arc chamber facility and program, our Indiana hypersonic integration facility and related programs, our Birmingham advanced manufacturing facility for hypersonic systems, expansion of our…

We also expect the continued build of our second lot of 12 capital Valkyrie aircraft, certain manufacturing and production related equipment for our recently acquired Nomad acquisition, certain other drone-related investments, our Vulcan, Kraken, Elysium, Nemesis and Hermes hypersonic initiatives, investments for our hypersonic related business, and other programs and initiatives.

Our 2026 and 2027 financial guidance and forecast also include our current estimated expenditures and timing of certain construction and procurement of certain machinery and equipment, and the potential for a reduction of certain of these planned expenditures, which have been or are expected to be funded under customer contracts.

Our forecast also includes the potential for a change in financial classification of certain investments or other items, including for various drone opportunities which may be classified either as a use of working capital in our Operating Cash Flow as work-in process or as capital expenditures when incurred, based on relevant facts and circumstances related to the items.

Following is our fourth quarter 2026, Full Year 2026 and initial Full Year 2027 financial forecast, which we potentially expect to update when we provide our Full year and Fourth quarter 2026 Report in late February 2027.

Similar to 2026 and previous years, as a result of a significant extended CR (which Kratos and our industry are currently operating under), we currently expect Kratos’ Fiscal 2027 Q1 to be our lowest in terms of Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, increasing in Q2 of 2027, with a significant increase in Q3 and a further increase in Q4 with an expected federal fiscal year 2027 budget appropriation in place.

We expect to provide FY27 operating and free cash flow guidance with our fourth quarter and full year 2026 financial report currently expected for late February 2027, once we have additional clarity on the current CR situation, additional insight into the timing of a federal fiscal year 2027 budget appropriation, and after the new Congress is seated.
